LESSON: PROPERTIES OF MATTER

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.1: Properties of matter
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Properties of matter, part of Matter in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: Why do we study the properties of matter?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Properties of matter together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner works with peers to carry out activities that show properties of matter

• Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology to observe the properties of the three states of matter.

Values:
• Unity: The learner collaborates with others when collecting different substances from the environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Heath Promotion Issues (preventive health): The learner avoids blowing air into the same balloon with others.

Link to other learning area:

• Mathematics: The learner uses the knowledge of properties of matter to measures the volume and mass of different

substances.

Suggested Learning Resources

Braille materials and equipment,

Digital devices with assistive technology such as adapted keyboards, screen readers and screen magnifiers,

Print materials in appropriate font and colour contrast,

Digital talking weighing balances,

Adapted apparatus for measuring volume.
